To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the sustainability of a regional urban water system can be assessed through the integration of supply, demand and adaptation indicators, b) regional water utilities can achieve sustainability through collaborative management practices that diversify their supply portfolios and c) regional management practices can lead to improved sustainability outcomes, including reduced supply costs, reduced water use, improved water quality, and reduced vulnerability to climate change.
a new paradigm for water management is required to achieve sustainability in coupled socio-hydraulic systems.

a regional integrative approach to water management, which includes the consideration of multiple supply and demand strategies and their interactions, is necessary for achieving sustainability of water resources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrative framework that can be used to assess water sustainability and inform the development of regional water management policies.
the development of a regional integrative sustainability framework that can help water agencies to assess their current sustainability and identify opportunities for sustainability improvements.
developing a regional integrative sustainability framework for water resource management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrates that a regional integrative approach to urban water sustainability is an effective and efficient strategy for achieving sustainability in coupled socio-hydologic systems.
the proposed framework provides a useful and practical tool for water managers to identify the sustainability level of their systems, and the opportunities to improve it.

the Hetch Hethcy Regional Water System (HHRWS) is currently operating at an overall water resource sustainability level of 0.68, which is below the threshold value of 0.8 that is considered sustainable by the proposed framework.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed framework can be applied to a variety of water management problems and that the results can be used to identify opportunities for improving sustainability.
the proposed framework provides an integrative tool to identify opportunities for improving the sustainability of regional water management systems.

a regional water sustainability index can be used as a decision support tool to identify opportunities for water management improvements and to prioritize investments in supply diversification projects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water agencies that are willing to collaborate can achieve long-term benefits by sharing resources, diversifying supply portfolios and improving their adaptive capacity.
a regional integrative approach to water management can provide a framework for the assessment, planning, and implementation of sustainable urban water systems.
water sustainability can be improved by increasing the adaptive capacity of the system through a more efficient use of the existing infrastructure.
